verses.text: Two days later there was a wedding in the town of Cana in Galilee. The mother of Jesus was there,
and Jesus and his followers had also been invited to the wedding.
When the wine ran out, Jesus' mother said to him, "They have no more wine."
Jesus replied, "Dear woman, why do you involve me? My time has not yet come."
His mother said to the servants, "Do whatever he tells you."
Six stone water jars were standing there. The Jewish people used them for their washing ceremonies. Each jar could hold between eighty and a hundred and twenty litres.
Jesus told the servants, "Fill the jars with water." So they filled them right to the top.
Then he told them, "Now pour some out and take it to the man in charge of the feast." So they did.
The man in charge tasted the water that had now become wine. He did not know where it had come from, but the servants who had poured the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside
and said to him, "Everyone serves the best wine first. Then, when the guests have had plenty to drink, they bring out the cheaper wine. But you have kept the best wine until now!"
This was the first of the miraculous signs that Jesus did. It happened in Cana in Galilee. In this way he showed his glory, and his followers believed in him.
After this, Jesus went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers and his followers. They stayed there for a few days.
It was nearly time for the Jewish Passover festival, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep and doves. Others were sitting at tables, exchanging money.
So Jesus made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple, together with the sheep and cattle. He scattered the coins of the money changers and turned over their tables.
He told those who were selling doves, "Get these things out of here! Stop turning my Father's house into a market!"
His followers remembered that the Scriptures say, "My love for your house burns in me like a fire."
Then the Jewish leaders asked him, "What miraculous sign can you show us to prove that you have the right to do this?"
Jesus answered, "Destroy this temple, and I will raise it up again in three days."
The leaders replied, "It has taken forty-six years to build this temple. Are you going to raise it up in three days?"
But the temple Jesus was speaking about was his own body.
After he was raised from the dead, his followers remembered that he had said this. Then they believed the Scriptures and the words that Jesus had spoken.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem for the Passover festival, many people saw the miraculous signs he was doing and believed in him.
But Jesus did not trust himself to them, because he knew what all people are like.
No one needed to tell him about anyone, because he knew what was really in each person's heart.
